intended_object: Takes a Cauchy sequence of complex numbers (for the complex absolute value) to the sequence of its real parts, packaged as a real Cauchy sequence (for the absolute value). Inferred from the docstring, and from its use in the completeness proof for ℂ (`limAux`, `lim_re`).
explanation:
The body is `⟨fun n ↦ (f n).re, isCauSeq_re f⟩`. This is the sequence of real parts of `f`, which is Cauchy because |Re w| ≤ |w|. That is exactly the intended object.

Mathlib also has a more general version, `RCLike.cauSeqRe`, for any `RCLike` field. That version cannot replace this one here. The `RCLike` class includes `CompleteSpace`, and `Complex.cauSeqRe` is one of the tools used to prove that ℂ is complete (through `limAux`, `isCauSeq_iff_lim`, `lim_re`), before ℂ gets its `RCLike` instance. So the special setting is forced by the order in which things are built, and the definition is not too narrow.

It is close to an auxiliary device for that completeness proof. Still, "the real part of a Cauchy sequence, as a Cauchy sequence" is a real mathematical construction, and it is formalized correctly.
